annotations.category_path: Supplemental Security Income / BUDGET INFORMATION / Adjustment for Date of Payment Shifta
annotations.variable_note: 20 C.F.R § 416.402 directs that if the first day of the month falls on a weekend or a holiday, the Social Security Administration will make Supplemental Security Income payments on the preceding business day. That will result in one additional payment in fiscal years 2028 and 2033 and one fewer payment in fiscal years 2029 and 2035.
annotations.source_label: Adjustment for Date of Payment Shifta

annotations.category_path: Supplemental Security Income / BUDGET INFORMATION / Total Outlays, Adjusted for Date of Payment Shiftb
annotations.variable_note: Adjusted amounts exclude the effects of shifting payments that otherwise would have been made on a weekend or holiday. For example, total outlays of $70.5 billion for fiscal year 2028 include 12 payments (those for October 2027 through September 2028). They do not include the thirteenth payment that will be made in that year (the payment for October 2028, which will made September 29, 2028; that payment is included in the $72.8 billion in outlays shown for fiscal year 2029).
annotations.source_label: Total Outlays, Adjusted for Date of Payment Shiftb
